title: Choose the look for the Navi website
question: The roll picked “Die Haltestelle” – the German bus stop as the page’s world. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Die Haltestelle
options.lineage: German bus & tram stops: the round H sign on its pole, the glass timetable case, the stop-name plate, DIN 1451 road-sign lettering
options.thesis: The website is a stop you walk up to: the sign says where you are, the case behind glass says what comes next. Refuses the app-landing template (headline, phone mockup, three feature cards).
options.viewport: A tall pole runs down the left edge; at its top the round stop disc carries the Navi mark. Beside it, the stop-name plate reads “Navi” in huge DIN, the line below names what it is. The glass case under it is a real, working mini departure board fed by the live API (Göttingen), with the Download APK action mounted like the case’s button.
options.risk: If the DIN type is set timidly or the case reads as a generic card, it collapses into the template it refuses.

raised.raise: Flat layered planes: pole, disc, plate and case are separate flat inks with real depth order, never gradients.
The shared-trip page advances like stops along the line: passed stops dim, the next stop is lit.

options.label: Bahnhofsbeschilderung
options.lineage: station wayfinding: dark-blue sign bands, platform-number cubes, pictograms
options.thesis: Navi as the signage that tells you where to go: every section a sign band, every fact a pictogram and a number.
options.viewport: A full-width sign band with “Navi →” and a huge platform cube; sections below are signs.
options.risk: The direction most transit sites land on; looks like an official DB product.

options.label: Travel poster planes
options.case: Fuses as a scenic Germany poster, but commuters do not identify with tourism; the offer gets hidden.
options.kept: Flat layered planes with strict depth order.

options.label: Darkroom stations
options.case: Nothing to do with getting around; amber flattens the live-status colours.
options.kept: Irreversible, ordered stations – the trip page’s passed/next stops.

options.label: Portrait plate
options.case: No relation to transit or its users.
options.kept: Captions with leader lines to what they name.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean app landing page (headline, phone screenshot, feature list), executed impeccably.
